thread:
mohit: heads-up — I ran the end-to-end perf pass on the FP8/INT8 prefill+decode flows for the 32k model and we have a strange regression on long contexts that looks quantization-related. TTFT for 32k prefill up ~35% on prod-like load.

cassie: rough numbers? is it prefill or decode blowup?

mohit: primarily prefill time. example: with static batching at 8 streams, prefill went from 420ms -> 560ms median. decode tail is slightly worse but decode TPS is OK. TTFT hit is surprising because we expected quantized prefill kernels to be faster.

kevin: do we have kernel selection logs for those runs? maybe runtime chose a fallback kernel (dequantize-heavy) for long sequences.

mohit: pasted the runtime decision snippet from the trace:  
```
[kernel-select] model: rwd-32k-quantized-v3
seq_len=32768 batch=1 path=host->fp8_avx fallback=INT8_dequantize_reason="calibration_mismatch"
selected_kernel=matmul_int8_deq->gemm_fp32_accel
```
kevin: ugh "calibration_mismatch" — that matches the calibration pass we added in v3 that does per-shard dynamic scale adjustment. the extra dequantize step kills memory streaming for big prefill matrices.

jen: did you capture nvprof/Nsight flame? that will show where the extra memcpy/dequantize is happening. also check KV cache behaviour — long prefill touches the cache a lot and quantized layouts can change access patterns.

mohit: nvprof snapshot attached in the CI artifact (link) but summary: 60% of added time is in kernel memcpy+dequantize on layernorm paths, 25% in scheduler stalls waiting for CUDA streams (lots of small async memcpy), rest is GEMM. KV cache shows extra page faults in the per-shard allocator under quant layout — small allocations for key/value slices are more fragmented.

sam: two questions: 1) is calibration executed at prefill time (per-request)? 2) are we falling back to a non-fused path for decode when context > X?

mohit: answers: 1) by default calibration is lazy-per-shard and can trigger on first prefill. in current experiment we had lazy calibration enabled. 2) yes, for seq > 16k the runtime currently marks some fused kernels as "unsafe" and picks a safe INT8 dequantize path.

cassie: so tradeoff: lazy calibration saves accuracy but penalizes TTFT for cold shards. for steady-state TPS we probably amortize it, but for interactive we lose. Could we pre-calibrate shards at deployment or during warmup?

kevin: proposal: two-prong approach — (A) prefer INT8 fused kernels for prefill if long context and batch>1 (maximize throughput), (B) prefer low-latency FP8/FP16 fused kernels for single-stream decode to minimize TTFT. Also add a fast-path that does a lightweight calibration estimate instead of full shard calibration.

jen: +1. I'd also suggest changing batching heuristics: currently continuous-batching groups by arrival time only. For long-context prefill we should prioritize forming larger batches (sacrifice a small extra enqueue delay) to use the throughput kernels and avoid per-request calibration hits. Add a policy knob: prefer_batch_for_prefill_threshold_ms.

sam: any quick experiments we can run? I can flip a runtime flag in staging to disable lazy-per-request calibration (force pre-calibrated weights) and re-run the 32k smoke.

mohit: yes please. also record kernel_select logs and nvprof. use `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_select,quant` and run: 
```
./run_inference_benchmark --model rwd-32k-quantized-v3 --seq 32768 --batch 8 --profile nvprof --warmup 50 --it 200
```
and a decode scenario: 
```
./run_inference_benchmark --mode decode --streams 1 --seq 32768 --profile nvprof --it 100
```

cassie: other angle — KV cache layout. If quantized KV uses smaller dtype packing (4-bit/INT8), our current allocator still uses 256B granularity leading to many small GPU mem transactions. We should change KV allocator to coalesce slices into larger blocks for long contexts. That will reduce memcpy overhead on prefill.

mohit: noted. I saw allocator coalescing was disabled for quantized weights due to alignment concerns; re-checking that.

kevin: let's also instrument TTFT vs TPS in the console per-route. TTFT is what users feel. Add two new metrics: prefill_TTFT_p50/p95 and decode_TTFT_p50/p95 under quantized variant. Then we can see which workloads are sensitive.

jen: will sketch the patch: 1) runtime flag to force pre-calibration (dev opt) 2) batching tweak for prefill preference 3) KV allocator coalescing for quant layouts 4) kernel selection rule change to prefer fused INT8 for prefill throughput. I'll open a draft PR and link perf numbers.

mohit: thanks — after we have the staging run results we'll decide if we revert the lazy calibration change or ship the allocator + kernel rule fixes. current suspicion: majority of regression is calibration + small-copy dequant path.

infra-bot: deploy: staging/rwd-quant-stress -> started by sam at 1767492065 : running benchmark (artifact will be uploaded to CI).

sam: started a run with `--no-lazy-calibration` now. will share artifacts. :thumbsup:

mohit: appreciated. if that cuts TTFT by >20% we can roll a hotfix to prod config while we land allocator changes.

cassie: also keep an eye on quality (perplexity/regression harness) — lightweight calibration might drift accuracy. we'll gate on eval thresholds.

kevin: OK next steps assigned: sam -> staging run + kernel_select logs, jen -> kernel/alloc PR sketch, cassie -> quality gating, mohIT -> perf dashboard TTFT/TPS metrics.

mohit: small note: typo in tasks, that's me (mohit lowercase) on dashboard. thanks everyone.
